---
title: "Writing and rendering experiments"
---

## Start a report

From the repository root:

```bash
cp experiments/templates/experiment.qmd experiments/reports/YYYY-MM-DD-short-name.qmd
```

Replace the title, date, description, categories, and placeholders. Keep one
report per question; update it as evidence arrives. Record unsuccessful results
and the decision they informed.

Use the training run's saved `config.yaml` for the resolved configuration and
its `git_hash` for the code version. Record dataset identity, split, selection
cuts, seed, checkpoint, and W&B URL. The current checkout's commit may differ
from the commit that produced a checkpoint. Include baseline provenance too.

Commit small, portable evaluation tables and figures beside the report, in a
matching subdirectory. Link them with relative paths. Keep ROOT files,
checkpoints, credentials, and large data outside Git; record their locations and
identifiers. A run directory alone does not identify a dataset version.

## Preview and build

Install the Quarto CLI using the [official installation instructions](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).
The CLI is separate from the Python dependencies managed by `uv`.

This workspace has Quarto 1.10.18 installed locally. To use it in your current
shell, run from the repository root:

```bash
export PATH="/home/degraw/deepsno/.local-tools/quarto-1.10.18/bin:$PATH"
```

The tool directory is ignored by Git; other checkouts need their own installation.

From the repository root:

```bash
quarto preview experiments
quarto render experiments
```

The rendered site is written to `experiments/_site/`. Templates are excluded
from rendering and the experiment listing.

## Computed analysis

Reports do not execute code by default, so a site build needs neither a GPU nor
cluster data. Run training and evaluation separately and report their saved
outputs. Existing notebooks can remain exploratory working documents.

For a report that needs executable Python, add this to its YAML header:

```yaml
jupyter: python3
execute:
  enabled: true
  freeze: true
```

Then explicitly execute that report with the project environment:

```bash
uv run quarto render experiments/reports/YYYY-MM-DD-short-name.qmd
```

Commit the resulting `experiments/_freeze/` files and any referenced figures.
Whole-project renders reuse frozen results; an individual report render
executes it again. Refresh deliberately when code, configuration, or input data
changes: freezing does not validate external inputs. See
[Quarto execution management](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html).

## GitHub Pages

The `Publish experiment journal` GitHub Actions workflow renders and deploys
this project when `experiments/`, `docs/`, or its workflow changes on `main`.
It can also be run manually from GitHub's Actions tab. It installs Quarto only;
reports use saved outputs and do not need the training environment.

In [repository Pages settings](https://github.com/scott-degraw/deepsno/settings/pages),
select **GitHub Actions** as the publishing source once. After a successful
deployment, the journal is available at
[scott-degraw.github.io/deepsno](https://scott-degraw.github.io/deepsno/).
The workflow includes the existing `docs/` event gallery at
[gallery/](https://scott-degraw.github.io/deepsno/gallery/).

Commit report sources, small figures, and any frozen analysis outputs, then
push to `main` to publish updates. The generated `_site/` is uploaded by CI
and stays out of Git. W&B links retain W&B's own access requirements.
